Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.

A firm operating in country S moved its existing capital equipment to a larger factory in country T. It also installed more of the same equipment and increased the size of its workforce. From the evidence provided, what must be true?

options.A: The firm is operating in the long run.
options.B: The firm is operating in the very long run.
options.C: The firm’s division of labour has increased.
options.D: The firm’s supply curve has shifted to the left.

questions.questionText: Which statement is not correct?

options.A: Addictive drugs are regarded as demerit goods because users are unaware of the full damage they do.
options.B: Air is regarded as a free good because its use has no opportunity cost.
options.C: National defence is regarded as a public good because one citizen ‘consuming’ it reduces the amount of it available to others.
options.D: Visits to a doctor are regarded as private goods partly because they are rival.

questions.questionText: The diagrams show production possibility curves. Which diagram shows constant opportunity costs?

options.A: B consumer consumer goods goods O O capital goods capital goods
options.C: D consumer consumer goods goods O O capital goods capital goods

questions.questionText: Farmers using traditional methods lack access to finance and often employ family members on a part-time basis. If working practices in agriculture could be improved, how would this be likely to be shown on the production possibility curve? R manufactured goods T S O agricultural goods

options.A: by a movement from R to T
options.B: by a movement from S to R
options.C: by a movement from S to T
options.D: by a movement from T to R

questions.questionText: In a particular year, 12000 units of a good are sold at $1 per unit. In a later year, 14000 units are sold at $1.20 per unit. If consumer tastes have remained constant, what could account for the change between the two years?

options.A: a decrease in the price of raw materials used by producers
options.B: an increase in the price of a substitute good
options.C: an increase in the rate of tax imposed on producers
options.D: the formation of a monopoly in the production of the good

questions.questionText: What is most likely to cause an increase in the consumer surplus in the market for a normal good?

options.A: an increase in consumer incomes
options.B: an increase in the number of substitute goods
options.C: an increase in the price of a complementary good
options.D: an increase in the price of the good

questions.questionText: The table shows Lee’s and Yim’s price elasticity of demand for restaurant meals and cinema tickets. Lee Yim restaurant meals –1.2 –0.8 cinema tickets –0.7 –1.3 There is a rise in the price of restaurant meals and a fall in the price of cinema tickets. What can be concluded after these price changes?

options.A: Restaurant owners will receive more income.
options.B: Lee will spend more money on both cinema tickets and restaurant meals.
options.C: Yim will spend more money on both cinema tickets and restaurant meals.
options.D: Cinema owners will receive less income.

questions.questionText: What is not held constant when aggregating individual firms’ supply curves to give the short-run market supply curve?

options.A: the number of firms in the industry
options.B: the price of the product
options.C: the prices of factors of production
options.D: the state of technology

questions.questionText: Which elasticity would a shortage of skilled workers affect?

options.A: cross elasticity of demand
options.B: income elasticity of demand
options.C: price elasticity of demand
options.D: price elasticity of supply

questions.questionText: D D shows an individual’s initial demand curve for public transport.
Which government action would be identified as the direct provision of goods and services?

options.A: increasing road maintenance because of poor weather conditions
options.B: making payments to low-income families with elderly dependents
options.C: subsidising firms in order to encourage them to increase their output
options.D: taxing firms because they have been emitting damaging fumes

questions.questionText: A specific tax is imposed on a product for which the elasticity of supply is zero. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The burden of this tax will fall entirely on consumers.
options.B: The burden of this tax will fall entirely on suppliers.
options.C: The burden of this tax will fall mainly on consumers.
options.D: The burden of this tax will fall mainly on suppliers.

questions.questionText: A government wishes to intervene in a free market to allocate healthcare at the socially optimal level. Which combination correctly identifies the reason for government intervention in the healthcare market? healthcare healthcare provision of consumption in a production in a information in a free market free market free market

options.A: overconsumption overproduction too little
options.B: overconsumption underproduction too much
options.C: underconsumption underproduction too little
options.D: underconsumption overproduction too much

questions.questionText: The table shows the Consumer Prices Index (CPI) for a country. year CPI 2008 100 2009 104 2010 102 2011 105 2012 108 2013 111 Which statement about the period 2008 to 2013 is correct?

options.A: Prices increased each year.
options.B: Prices increased fastest in 2011.
options.C: The rate of inflation was 2% in 2010.
options.D: The smallest rise in prices was in 2013.

questions.questionText: What is most likely to cause the price level to rise? An increase in

options.A: productivity of labour.
options.B: raw material prices.
options.C: income taxes.
options.D: subsidies paid to producers.

questions.questionText: What is most likely to increase a country’s circular flow of income?

options.A: Its budget deficit increases.
options.B: Its imports increase.
options.C: Its interest rates increase.
options.D: Its exchange rate increases.

questions.questionText: A country with a constant population experiences a 5% increase in its nominal GDP during a year. In which situation will average living standards be most likely to have increased during the year?

options.A: if government takes action to ensure there is no increase in unemployment
options.B: if inflation during the year is 3%
options.C: if there is no increase in real national income
options.D: if there is no redistribution of income

questions.questionText: Which combination correctly identifies the necessary information to construct an accurately labelled graph of a normal short-run aggregate supply curve (SRAS)? gradient of the horizontal x-axis vertical y-axis SRAS curve

options.A: negative quantity price level
options.B: positive real output price level
options.C: positive real output price
options.D: positive price level real output

questions.questionText: A government makes two changes to income tax.
Which supply-side policy is most likely to decrease a government’s budget deficit?

options.A: cutting tax rates on company profits
options.B: cutting unemployment benefits
options.C: raising spending on education and training
options.D: raising tax-free income tax allowances

questions.questionText: Which combination of fiscal and monetary policies would certainly be expansionary? government money taxes spending supply

options.A: decrease decrease decrease
options.B: decrease increase decrease
options.C: increase decrease increase
options.D: increase increase increase

questions.questionText: The central bank of a country raises interest rates to reduce the general price level. When is this policy likely to have the biggest impact? position of the economy responsiveness of on its production possibility aggregate demand to curve (PPC) diagram interest rate changes

options.A: below the PPC high
options.B: below the PPC low
options.C: on the PPC high
options.D: on the PPC low

questions.questionText: The table shows the trade in goods and services for an economy between 2019 and 2021. trade in goods year and services ($ millions) 2019 –1000 2020 –3000 2021 –4000 What would have most likely caused the change from 2019 to 2021?

options.A: increasing domestic unemployment
options.B: increasing domestic rate of income tax
options.C: increasing domestic inflation
options.D: increasing import tariffs

questions.questionText: A government subsidises training to improve the skills of workers in the industrial sector of an economy. What is the most likely effect on the current account of the balance of payments?

options.A: exports fall
options.B: exports rise
options.C: imports fall
options.D: imports rise

questions.questionText: Using all their resources efficiently, country X can produce 6 million tonnes of wheat or 2 million tonnes of steel whilst country Y can produce 4 million tonnes of wheat or 1 million tonnes of steel. Based on this information, what does the theory of comparative advantage suggest?

options.A: Country X should produce only steel.
options.B: Country X will not gain from international trade.
options.C: Country Y has no comparative advantage.
options.D: Country Y will not gain from international trade.

questions.questionText: Countries X and Y are trade partners. An increase in which economic indicator in country Y is most likely to cause a fall in the exchange rate of country X?

options.A: economic growth
options.B: inflation rate
options.C: money supply
options.D: trade barriers

questions.questionText: Which transaction is not recorded in the current account?

options.A: aid received from the government of another country
options.B: exports of raw materials
options.C: investments by a foreign company
options.D: payments of dividends to an overseas investor

questions.questionText: A government decides to place a tariff on imports of raw materials. Which statement about the impact of the tariff is correct?

options.A: It will increase costs of production for domestic firms.
options.B: It will increase consumer surplus for domestic consumers.
options.C: It will reduce government revenue.
options.D: There will be a fall in the price of imports and a rise in the demand.

questions.questionText: In which situation will a country’s terms of trade improve?

options.A: Its imports rise in value less than its exports.
options.B: Its imports rise in volume less than its exports.
options.C: The price of its imports rises by less than the prices of its exports.
